questions.question_text: A $6$-pack of eggs costs $\$2.55$ and an $8$-pack costs $\$3.50$. What is the cost per egg of the better buy?

options.why: This is the unit price of the $8$-pack, which is the dearer option per egg.
Averaged the two unit prices instead of choosing the lower one.
Divided $\$2.55$ by $8$, mixing the price of one offer with the size of the other.

questions.solution_text:
Option 1: $\dfrac{\$2.55}{6\text{ eggs}} = \dfrac{\$0.425}{1\text{ egg}}$
Option 2: $\dfrac{\$3.50}{8\text{ eggs}} = \dfrac{\$0.4375}{1\text{ egg}}$
$\$0.425 < \$0.4375$, so the better buy costs $\$0.4250$ per egg.

questions.question_text: Sugar is sold in four different sized packets. Which is the best buy?

options.why: Chose the largest packet, but $\$6.90 \div 2 = \$3.45$ per kg is dearer than $\$3.30$ per kg.
Chose the lowest total price, but $\$0.40$ for $100$ g is $\$4.00$ per kg — the dearest option.
Read the price straight off the $1$ kg packet without comparing the other packets per kilogram.

questions.solution_text:
$100$ g: $\dfrac{\$0.40}{0.1\text{ kg}} = \dfrac{\$4.00}{1\text{ kg}}$
$500$ g: $\dfrac{\$1.65}{0.5\text{ kg}} = \dfrac{\$3.30}{1\text{ kg}}$
$1$ kg: $\dfrac{\$3.50}{1\text{ kg}}$
$2$ kg: $\dfrac{\$6.90}{2\text{ kg}} = \dfrac{\$3.45}{1\text{ kg}}$
$\$3.30$ is the lowest, so $500$ g for $\$1.65$ is the best buy.

questions.question_text: Coffee is sold in a $200$ g jar for $\$1.55$, a $0.5$ kg jar for $\$3.70$ and a $750$ g jar for $\$5.70$. Which is the best buy?

options.why: At $\$7.60$ per kg this is cheaper than the $200$ g jar but dearer than the $0.5$ kg jar.
Chose the lowest total price; per kilogram it is the dearest at $\$7.75$.

options.text: The $0.5$ kg jar and the $750$ g jar are equally good value
options.why: Treats $0.5$ kg as $50$ g or $5000$ g, so the two unit prices come out equal.

questions.question_text: Chips are sold in a $45$ g bag for $\$2.10$ and a $150$ g bag for $\$6.50$. Comparing grams per dollar, which is the best buy?

options.text: The $150$ g bag, which gives $23.1$ g per $\$1$
The $45$ g bag, which gives $21.4$ g per $\$1$
options.why: Picked the smaller grams-per-dollar figure; with units per dollar the higher value is better.

options.text: The $150$ g bag, which gives $2.3$ g per $\$1$
options.why: Divided $150$ by $65$ instead of by $6.50$, shifting the answer by a factor of ten.

options.text: The $45$ g bag, which gives $94.5$ g per $\$1$
options.why: Multiplied $45$ by $2.10$ instead of dividing to get the amount per dollar.

questions.solution_text:
Option 1: $\dfrac{45\text{ g}}{\$2.10} = \dfrac{21.4\text{ g}}{\$1}$
Option 2: $\dfrac{150\text{ g}}{\$6.50} = \dfrac{23.1\text{ g}}{\$1}$
More grams per dollar is better value, so the $150$ g bag is the best buy.

questions.question_text: Flour is sold in $2$ kg bags for $\$3.40$ and in $5$ kg bags for $\$8.25$. What does $10$ kg of flour cost from each option, and which is the best buy?

options.why: Costed both correctly but then chose the dearer total for the same $10$ kg.
Multiplied the $2$ kg bag price by $2$ instead of by the $5$ bags that $10$ kg needs.
Multiplied each bag price by $10$ instead of by the number of bags needed for $10$ kg.

questions.solution_text:
Option 1: $10 \div 2 = 5$ bags
$5 \times \$3.40 = \$17.00$
Option 2: $10 \div 5 = 2$ bags
$2 \times \$8.25 = \$16.50$
For the same $10$ kg the $5$ kg bags cost less, so the $5$ kg bag is the best buy.

questions.question_text: Iced tea is sold as $250$ mL for $\$2.00$, $600$ mL for $\$4.20$ and $1$ L for $\$7.50$. Which bottle is the best buy?

options.why: Chose the lowest total price, but at $\$8.00$ per litre it is the dearest per unit.
Assumed the largest bottle must be best; at $\$7.50$ per litre it is beaten by the $600$ mL bottle.

options.text: The $250$ mL and $1$ L bottles are equally good value
options.why: Compared $\$2.00$ per $250$ mL with $\$7.50$ per $1$ L without converting millilitres to litres, so no unit price was actually found.

questions.solution_text:
$250$ mL: $\dfrac{\$2.00}{0.25\text{ L}} = \dfrac{\$8.00}{1\text{ L}}$
$600$ mL: $\dfrac{\$4.20}{0.6\text{ L}} = \dfrac{\$7.00}{1\text{ L}}$
$1$ L: $\dfrac{\$7.50}{1\text{ L}}$
$\$7.00$ is the lowest price per litre, so the $600$ mL bottle is the best buy.

questions.question_text: A supermarket sells $400$ g tins of soup for $\$3.60$ each with a "buy $2$, get $1$ free" offer. A rival shop sells a $1.2$ kg family tin for $\$9.00$. Which shop is the better value?

options.text: The rival shop, at $\$7.50$ per kg
options.why: Priced the supermarket at $\$9.00$ per kg by paying for all three tins and ignoring the free one.
Treated one $400$ g tin as a full kilogram, understating the supermarket's true price per kilogram.

options.text: The rival shop, at $\$3.00$ per kg
options.why: Divided $\$9.00$ by $3$ tins' worth of soup rather than by the $1.2$ kg the family tin contains.

questions.solution_text:
Supermarket, taking the offer: $3 \times 400\text{ g} = 1.2$ kg for $2 \times \$3.60 = \$7.20$
$\dfrac{\$7.20}{1.2\text{ kg}} = \dfrac{\$6.00}{1\text{ kg}}$
Rival shop: $\dfrac{\$9.00}{1.2\text{ kg}} = \dfrac{\$7.50}{1\text{ kg}}$
$\$6.00 < \$7.50$, so the supermarket is the better value.
